Complete Empirical Research Plan  

====================================================  
1. Identification Strategy  
----------------------------------------------------  
Chosen design: Difference-in-Differences (DiD) implemented on a narrow band of firms around the SEC’s $75 million public-float cutoff, supplemented with a fuzzy Regression-Discontinuity (RD) robustness check that instruments actual Section 404 compliance with the cutoff indicator.  

Why DiD?  
• The reform went into force at a clearly defined date (FY 2004 year-ends on/after 15 Nov 2004).  
• Firms just above the $75 m threshold (“accelerated filers”) were forced to adopt Section 404 one to five years earlier than observationally similar firms just below the line.  
• Using pre-reform years 2002-2003 as the baseline and post-reform 2004-2007 as the treatment window allows us to difference out common macro/accounting trends.  
• Because assignment is mechanical (public float), selection on unobservables is unlikely within a tight band, making parallel-trends more credible.  

The companion fuzzy RD checks that the discontinuity in public float generates a large jump in the probability of compliance and uses that jump as an instrument for compliance intensity (auditor attestation obtained or not).  

====================================================  
2. Treatment and Control Definitions  
----------------------------------------------------  
Treatment variable  
TREAT_i = 1 if firm i’s SEC-determined public float in fiscal year t-1 is ≥ $75 million (accelerated filer), 0 otherwise.  

Control group  
Firms with public float in a symmetric bandwidth around the cutoff that remain < $75 m (e.g., $50–74.9 m).  

Sample restriction for baseline DiD  
$50 m ≤ PublicFloat_{t-1} ≤ $100 m so that treated and control firms are of very similar size.  

Treatment timing / event date  
First treated year: fiscal years ending on or after 15 Nov 2004 (our data flags FY 2004 because most firms in sample have Dec year-ends).  
Pre-period: FY 2002–2003.  
Post-period: FY 2004–2007.  

Running variable and cutoff for RD robustness  
Running var: Log(PublicFloat_{t-1}).  
Cutoff: log(75 m).  
Compliance probability jumps from ≈0 to ≈1 at that point, but imperfectly (hence fuzzy).  

====================================================  
3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
----------------------------------------------------  
A1. Parallel trends: In the absence of Section 404, above- and below-cutoff firms would have experienced similar trends in audit fees, earnings conservatism, and Tobin’s q.  
Plausibility: Within a $50–100 m band, firms face similar macro shocks, industry trends, and financing constraints. We can bolster this by showing pre-period parallel-trend tests and adding firm & year FEs.  

A2. No manipulation of the running variable: Managers could not precisely manage public float to avoid accelerated-filer status in 2002-2004.  
Plausibility: Public float is driven by market prices and share count, both hard to fine-tune around exactly $75 m, especially ex-ante in 2002 when the threshold’s consequences were not fully known. We will test for bunching using McCrary density tests.  

A3. Stable composition: Entry/exit around the cutoff is not systematically affected by Section 404 during the sample window.  
Plausibility: Delistings and IPO activity are low in this narrow size range. We can check attrition patterns.  

A4. No other contemporaneous policy targeting only accelerated filers in 2004 that independently affects outcomes.  
Plausibility: SOX Sections 302 & 906, NYSE/NASDAQ governance rules, etc. applied to all listed firms; no other initiative targets the ≥ $75 m float group exclusively.  

====================================================  
4. Most Important Threats and Mitigation  
----------------------------------------------------  
Threat 1: Non-parallel pre-trends (violating A1).  
Mitigation: (i) Plot outcomes 2000–2003 to document trends; (ii) include firm-specific linear time trends; (iii) run event-study DiD with leads to show no pre-treatment effects.  

Threat 2: Sorting/manipulation at the cutoff (violating A2).  
Mitigation: McCrary density test; balance checks of covariates just above/below cutoff; if manipulation detected, rely on DiD bandwidths that exclude manipulated region, or switch to fuzzy RD IV.  

Threat 3: Differential macro shocks post-2004 that hit slightly larger firms harder (e.g., Section 404 interacted with industry demand changes).  
Mitigation: Industry-year fixed effects; allow heterogeneous trends by interacting industry dummies with time; conduct placebo analysis using an earlier pseudo-cutoff year (e.g., pretend the rule started in 2001).  

====================================================  
5. R Code Outline (simplified)  
----------------------------------------------------  
```r
# 0. Packages -------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)      # fast data wrangling
library(fixest)          # high-dim FE regressions
library(rdrobust)        # RD estimation
library(ggplot2)         # visuals

# 1. Load data -----------------------------------------------
audit <- fread("audit_fees.csv")          # Audit Analytics
comp  <- fread("compustat.csv")           # Compustat
crsp  <- fread("crsp_monthly.csv")        # CRSP
float <- fread("public_float_hand.csv")   # hand-collected
status<- fread("mgmt_report_status.csv")  # 10-K hand data

# 2. Merge & Clean -------------------------------------------
dat <- Reduce(function(x,y) merge(x,y, all=TRUE,
               by=c("gvkey","fyear")), 
               list(audit, comp, float, status))

# keep non-financials, 2002-2007
dat <- dat[!sic %between% c(6000,6999) & fyear %in% 2002:2007]

# 3. Construct Key Vars --------------------------------------
dat[, treat  := as.integer(public_float_lag >= 75)]
dat[, post   := as.integer(fyear >= 2004)]
dat[, did    := treat*post]

# outcomes
dat[, ln_auditfee := log(audit_fee)]
dat[, consrv      := abs(discretionary_accruals)]   # earnings conservatism proxy
dat[, tobins_q    := (mve + at - ceq)/at ]          # simple q

# controls (size, leverage, etc.)
dat[, ln_assets  := log(at)]
dat[, lev        := dltt/at]

# 4. Main DiD Regression -------------------------------------
# Firm and year FE; clustered SEs at gvkey
feols_main <- feols(ln_auditfee ~ did + ln_assets + lev |
                    gvkey + fyear, data=dat, cluster="gvkey")
summary(feols_main)

# 5. Event-study robustness ----------------------------------
es <- feols(ln_auditfee ~ i(fyear, treat, ref=2003) + 
            ln_assets + lev | gvkey + fyear, 
            data=dat, cluster="gvkey")
iplot(es)  # visual check of pre-trends

# 6. Fuzzy RD IV robustness ----------------------------------
# Narrow ±40 % band around 75 m
rd <- dat[public_float_lag %between% c(45,105) & fyear==2004]
rdrobust(y=rd$ln_auditfee, x=rd$public_float_lag - 75, fuzzy=rd$treat)

# 7. Placebo DiD (pseudo-reform 2001) ------------------------
dat[, post_pseudo := as.integer(fyear >= 2001)]
dat[, did_pseudo  := treat*post_pseudo]
feols(ln_auditfee ~ did_pseudo + ln_assets + lev |
      gvkey + fyear, data=dat[fyear<=2003],
      cluster="gvkey")
```

====================================================  
6. Expected Results (Economic Priors)  
----------------------------------------------------  
Audit fees: Positive and sizable. Prior literature suggests SOX 404 roughly doubled audit fees for small firms. I expect a log-point increase of 0.6–0.9 (≈ 80 % hike).  

Earnings conservatism: Increase in absolute discretionary accruals should fall (i.e., accruals become more timely, less aggressive). Expect −0.01 to −0.02 change in discretionary accruals scaled by assets.  

Market valuation (Tobin’s q): Net effect ambiguous. For small firms, compliance costs probably outweigh improved credibility initially; anticipate a drop of 0.05–0.10 in q.  

====================================================  
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DiD)  
----------------------------------------------------  
C1: Parallel pre-trends demonstrated (will test)…………………1  
C2: No simult. shocks differentially affecting groups…………0.5  
C3: No manipulation around cutoff…………………………………0.5  
C4: Stable composition / no differential attrition……………1  
C5: Treatment exogenous within bandwidth………………………1  

Aggregate score: 4 / 5 (some remaining concern over C2 & C3).
